note: The CLOSED table of Candidate-level DISCLOSURE-CLASS fields and the owner
surface each one reaches (kogaki#909, owner ruling 2026-09-06).
A disclosure-class field is Harness-written evidence ABOUT a Candidate
that the owner is owed sight of. Before this table each such field
re-derived the same absence in its own paragraph - the bridge disclosure
did, the revise residue did, and #877's `figure:` would have been the
third - so the class is decided here once instead of a fourth time.
THE TEST IS WHETHER THE EVIDENCE BEARS ON THE CHOICE. Evidence that bears
on the pending selection is `decision` grade and reaches the selection
gate, because a pending human verdict's carrier is the render layer: the
owner acts on what they see and not on what the record contains. Evidence
that is a post-hoc report or approval is `post-hoc` grade and rides the
minted Brief's slot, because nothing is owed about a path not taken.

CLOSED means a field enters by editing this file under its own issue. The
surface is not optional and not inferable: a grade names one surface, and
src/assemble.mjs refuses a Candidate carrying a `decision`-grade field
that its option composition did not render. That refusal is why field N+1
cannot repeat the defect - it fails the same assertion rather than
needing a check member of its own.
This is NOT a claim that an undeclared field is detected. The table binds
the fields the Harness writes; a composer inventing a key nothing renders
is outside its reach, and that bound is stated here rather than left for
a reader to discover by trusting the guard too far.

bridges.why: §4.11 approves a Bridge Step by disclosing it after the fact. The approval is about what was ADOPTED, so a per-Candidate disclosure was always wider than the thing approved (kogaki#864, built at kogaki#866).

revise_residue.why: It says this Candidate spent its one revise round and that anything the revise did not repair stands. That is a property of the Candidate the owner is choosing BETWEEN, so it is owed before the choice rather than after it (kogaki#894, carried at kogaki#909).
